title: Ken-Burns_Zoom
slide_intent: Move a still image subtly so it feels active without forcing the viewer to track a new subject.
strategic_value: A slow zoom can give DB photography life while preserving attention on the employee.
demonstration: An employee photograph gradually changes scale; a small inward-corner indicator appears at the lower left.
practical_value: Choose a slow zoom when closer framing strengthens the existing subject.

content_islands.name: Photograph
content_islands.spec: Keep the employee as the visual anchor while changing image scale.

content_islands.name: Zoom indicator
content_islands.spec: Place the small corner-shaped cue at the lower left.

reference_purposes.Intent: Accompanying Ken-Burns prose explains that slow zooms or pans give still images more dynamism and make content feel more alive.
